hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to a distinct, high-contrast, and typically rectangular or compact geometric region—such as a label, screen, patch, sheet of paper, square cutout, or logo—superimposed against a darker, textured background. The activating feature is characterized by its sharp definition and relatively uniform high luminosity or lightness compared to the surrounding area. This pattern is robust to variations in semantic content (ranging from digital screens and product labels to biological forms and negative space), specific material textures, and surface orientation. The spatial arrangement consistently places the bright feature in the center or upper-middle of the frame, typically occupying 15–40% of the image area. The activating feature is invariably light-colored—specifically white, beige, bright yellow, cyan, or metallic gold—contrasted against a background of dark grey, black, deep brown, or olive green, creating a strict light-on-dark polarity.
